items.title: Larry Gold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2025
items.q: The interviewee discusses Fred Wesley's comments about writing for James Brown, but does not mention any personal interaction or relationship with James Brown himself.

ctx.x: I like working, I like music, I like — been doing this since I was a little boy. It's the thing I do best actually I think. I think at this point I do this better than playing the cello even though at one time I think I played the cello better than I did this. So I think what happened was they got reversed. And I'm always fascinated, like this year I guess I can say I did a really nice song with Ed Sheeran that'll come out in September. It's like sort of like a wedding song in an R&B style and it was a good song.…

I read a quote from let's see, who said it — Fred Wesley, when I spoke to him. He said this phrase probably six times in the interview talking about writing for James Brown he said, "I didn't know what I was doing." And he kept saying it, like — and I felt like saying, "Well yes you did." But have you ever been in a situation early on that you didn't feel like you knew what you were doing?

Absolutely. You learn on the job. That's what Fred means. But Fred was a great player. And he knew all about that stuff, he had grown up listening to those records. Come on. You know? But yeah I mean my early on I would look for — I would wait for Tommy Bell to smile or Gamble & Huff to say damn that's nice or McFadden and Whitehead to come in and start dancing in the studio in front of the strings. You know? All of a sudden I said, "I take it you like it." They said, "Yeah we do." I mean Whitehead used to call…
